explanation: The theorem says that the pushforward of a Haar measure on the unipotent subgroup (the range of unipotentGL2Hom) of GL₂(K) under the library-defined `entry` map is an additive Haar measure on K. The statement is tied to the library's own definitions `entry` and `unipotentGL2Hom`. The proof uses the library's `entry_ofEntry_mul`, together with `map_map` and `map_mul_left_eq_self`. Mathlib has general results that a continuous surjective group hom pushes a Haar measure to a Haar measure (`isHaarMeasure_map` and its `Add` analogue). I did not apply them, because `entry` is not stated as a hom. It goes from a multiplicative subgroup to an additive group, so a derivation would first have to build a `MulEquiv` to `Multiplicative K`. That, plus the instance bookkeeping, would take more than two short lines. I found no Mathlib declaration that matches directly or as a short special case. I did not run searches over Mathlib. This verdict rests on reading the library file and on my recollection of Mathlib's Haar-measure API.
